boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten documented stops on Georgetown’s downtown walking-tour corridors, each with a distinct architectural or local-history detail to look for.

cards.title: Historic Williamson County Courthouse: inspect the copper dome
cards.subtitle: Austin Avenue corridor, downtown Georgetown
cards.notes: Circle the courthouse grounds and look up at the copper dome, Ionic-columned porticoes, pediments, and balustrade described by the walking-tour record.
cards.short_summary: A 1911 Beaux Arts courthouse and the walking tour’s central civic landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Preservation Georgetown identifies this 1911 C. H. Page-designed courthouse as the focal point of the central business district and documents its copper dome and Ionic porticoes.
cards.source_title: Historic Williamson County Courthouse | Preservation Georgetown
cards.access_notes: Use the exterior grounds and follow posted access rules for the building.

cards.title: Palace Theatre: spot the Art Deco façade
cards.subtitle: Austin Avenue corridor, downtown Georgetown
cards.notes: Pause outside to photograph the flat and three-dimensional Art Deco motifs; check the theatre’s own schedule separately before planning a performance.
cards.short_summary: A 1925 theatre remodeled into its present Art Deco appearance in 1936.
cards.evidence_claim: Preservation Georgetown says the Palace was built in 1925, remodeled to its present Art Deco appearance in 1936, and rehabilitated as a community performing-arts center in the 1990s.
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is the reliable option; performance access depends on the theatre’s schedule and ticketing.

cards.title: Steele Store & Makemson Hotel: trace the early commercial corner
cards.subtitle: West 8th Street corridor, downtown Georgetown
cards.notes: Read the building as a layered corner: the record traces uses here from a hotel and stage stop to dry goods, banking, hotel, retail, and professional space.
cards.short_summary: A restored limestone commercial complex with documented uses reaching back to 1848.
cards.evidence_claim: Preservation Georgetown documents commercial activity at this corner from 1848 and says rehabilitation begun in 1981 helped inspire downtown Georgetown’s revitalization.
cards.source_title: Steele Store & Makemson Hotel | Preservation Georgetown
cards.access_notes: View the historic exterior from the public sidewalk; individual tenant access varies.

cards.title: Farmers State Bank Building: find the recovered brickwork
cards.subtitle: South Austin Avenue corridor, downtown Georgetown
cards.notes: Look across the storefront and compare its layered façade with the record’s account of early brickwork found beneath a later stucco veneer.
cards.short_summary: A 1910 bank building later used for county offices and museum space.
cards.evidence_claim: Preservation Georgetown says the current building was completed in 1910 and that historic brickwork was discovered beneath a mid-20th-century stucco veneer.
cards.source_title: Farmers State Bank Building (1910) | Preservation Georgetown
cards.access_notes: View the façade from the sidewalk; confirm museum or office access directly with the occupant.

cards.title: M.B. Lockett Building: study the Victorian storefront
cards.subtitle: West 7th Street corridor, downtown Georgetown
cards.notes: Stand back far enough to pick out the cast-iron columns, oriel window, and pressed-metal cornice that distinguish this High Victorian commercial building.
cards.short_summary: A restored 1896 High Victorian commercial building tied to a longtime Southwestern trustee.
cards.evidence_claim: Preservation Georgetown describes the M.B. Lockett Building as a High Victorian commercial example with cast-iron columns, an oriel window, and pressed-metal cornice; it notes Lockett served as a Southwestern trustee for 27 years.
cards.access_notes: Exterior architectural viewing from the public sidewalk is appropriate; tenant access varies.

cards.entity_name: Fire House and Old City Hall
cards.title: Fire House and Old City Hall: locate the original fire bell
cards.subtitle: South Main Street corridor, downtown Georgetown
cards.notes: Walk the building’s edge and look for the original fire bell above the pocket-park area, where the former water-tower footprint is documented.
cards.short_summary: An 1892 limestone civic building built for Georgetown’s volunteer fire department and municipal operations.
cards.evidence_claim: Preservation Georgetown says this 1892 structure housed the Hook and Ladder Company and municipal operations, and that the standpipe perimeter remains visible beneath the original fire bell.
cards.source_title: Fire House and Old City Hall (1892) | Preservation Georgetown
cards.access_notes: Use the sidewalk and adjacent public pocket-park area; do not enter restricted portions.

cards.title: Grace Heritage Center: photograph the Gothic details
cards.subtitle: South Main Street corridor, downtown Georgetown
cards.notes: From Founders Memorial Park, frame the pointed-arch and diamond-shaped windows, stained glass, and tower finials of this restored former sanctuary.
cards.short_summary: Georgetown’s oldest wood-frame religious structure, now preserved at its current downtown site.
cards.evidence_claim: Preservation Georgetown identifies Grace Heritage Center as the city’s oldest wood-frame religious structure and documents its Gothic Revival windows, stained glass, and tower detailing.
cards.access_notes: View the exterior and park setting; event or interior access is scheduled separately.

cards.title: Old U.S. Post Office: add a federal-era façade to the walk
cards.subtitle: East 8th Street corridor, downtown Georgetown
cards.notes: Use the tour’s red QR markers to identify this 1931 stop, then compare its form with the neighboring older commercial buildings on the Square.
cards.short_summary: A named 1931 stop on Preservation Georgetown’s self-guided downtown route.
cards.evidence_claim: Preservation Georgetown lists the Old U.S. Post Office (1931) as a stop on its self-guided Downtown Walking Tour of the Square and nearby blocks.
cards.access_notes: Follow the self-guided tour from public sidewalks and scan any posted red QR marker.

cards.title: Old Williamson County Jail: make it a QR-tour stop
cards.subtitle: East 7th Street corridor, downtown Georgetown
cards.notes: Find the tour’s red QR marker at this named 1888 landmark and use the linked interpretation to place the jail within the surrounding historic blocks.
cards.short_summary: An 1888 jail listed among the named landmarks on the downtown self-guided route.
cards.evidence_claim: Preservation Georgetown lists the Old Williamson County Jail (1888) as a named stop on its Downtown Walking Tour.
cards.access_notes: View from public rights-of-way and follow any onsite restrictions.

cards.title: Old Railroad Produce Warehouse: end on a rail-history landmark
cards.subtitle: Rock Street corridor, downtown Georgetown
cards.notes: Use the final historic stop as a reason to walk beyond the Square; scan its red QR marker for the site’s interpretation and photograph the warehouse exterior.
cards.short_summary: A named 1904 warehouse stop on the documented downtown walking-tour route.
cards.evidence_claim: Preservation Georgetown lists the Old Railroad Produce Warehouse (1904) as a named stop on its self-guided Downtown Walking Tour.
cards.access_notes: Use public sidewalks and observe posted access restrictions around the property.
